subject: maths
title: Advanced 8 · Test 2
summary: A second 15-question test on comparing data sets, two-step chance experiments, and Venn diagrams and two-way tables.
body:
This second test covers Advanced 8: comparing data sets (centre, spread, outliers and working backwards from the mean), two-step chance experiments (tables, tree diagrams, with and without replacement) and Venn diagrams and two-way tables.

There are 15 multiple-choice questions. Allow about 25 minutes, with no notes and no calculator unless the question says. Show your working on paper — many questions need two or three steps. Read every diagram and table carefully: check the scale, the totals and exactly which group the question is asking about. When you finish, check each answer makes sense in context.

questions.prompt: Using the Venn diagram (ξ = 30), how many items are in A or B (or both)?
questions.explanation: A or B = only A + both + only B = 10 + 6 + 9 = 25. Leaving out the overlap gives 19.
steps: "A or B" means inside at least one circle.
Add the three regions inside the circles: 10 + 6 + 9 = 25.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you left out the 6 in the overlap. "Or" includes items in both sets.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you added the circle totals (16 + 15), which counts the overlap twice.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 5 is the number in neither set — the opposite of what is asked.

questions.diagram_alt: A Venn diagram with ξ = 30. Only A: 10. A and B: 6. Only B: 9. Neither: 5.

questions.prompt: Team X scored 5, 7, 8, 8, 12 points in five games. Team Y scored 2, 6, 8, 11, 13. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Team Y is better, because its highest score is bigger.
options.B: The medians are equal, but Team X is more consistent.
options.C: Team X is better, because its range is smaller.
options.D: The teams are exactly the same, because their medians are equal.

questions.explanation: Both medians are 8, so the teams are equal on a typical game; Team X's range (7) is smaller than Team Y's (11), so X is more consistent. A smaller range does not mean "better".
steps: Same median, and X has the smaller range, so X is more consistent.

mistakes.A: Step 1: one high score does not make a team better on average — compare the medians.
mistakes.C: Step 2: a smaller range means more consistent, not a higher typical score. The medians are equal.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the ranges (7 and 11) are different, so the teams are not the same.

questions.prompt: The spinner has three equal sections numbered 1, 2 and 3. It is spun twice and the two numbers are added. What is the probability that the total is 4?
questions.explanation: There are 3 × 3 = 9 outcomes, and (1, 3), (2, 2) and (3, 1) total 4: 3/9 = 1/3. Treating the totals as equally likely gives 1/5.

mistakes.B: Step 1: the five totals 2 to 6 are not equally likely. List the 9 outcomes instead.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you missed (2, 2). There are three ways to make 4.
mistakes.D: Step 2: (1, 3) and (3, 1) are different outcomes, and (2, 2) works too.

questions.diagram_alt: A spinner divided into three equal sections labelled 1, 2 and 3.

questions.prompt: The dot plots show Group 1 and Group 2. How much bigger is the median of Group 2 than the median of Group 1?
questions.explanation: Each group has 6 values, so the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: Group 1 (6 + 6) ÷ 2 = 6, Group 2 (7 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.5. The difference is 1.5.
steps: Each group has 6 values, so the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th values.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 2 is the difference between the modes (8 and 6). Use the medians.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 0 is the difference between the ranges (both 6). Use the medians.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 7.5 is the median of Group 2 on its own. Subtract the median of Group 1.

questions.diagram_alt: Parallel dot plots from 0 to 10. Group 1: dots at 3, 5, 6, 6, 7 and 9. Group 2: dots at 4, 6, 7, 8, 8 and 10.

questions.prompt:
The table shows 50 families:

| | Pet | No pet | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| **House** | 26 | 8 | 34 |
| **Apartment** | 6 | 10 | 16 |
| **Total** | 32 | 18 | 50 |

One family is chosen at random from all 50. What is the probability that it lives in an apartment and has no pet?
questions.explanation: Apartment and no pet is one cell: 10. Out of all 50 families, P = 10/50 = 1/5. Dividing by 16 would only be right if we knew the family lived in an apartment.
steps: "Apartment and no pet" is the cell where that row and column meet: 10.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you divided by the apartment total (16). The family is chosen from all 50.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you divided by the "no pet" total (18). The family is chosen from all 50.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 16/50 is every apartment family. "And no pet" narrows it to one cell.

questions.prompt: A captain and a vice-captain are chosen from 5 players. The same player cannot be both. How many different ways can this be done?
questions.explanation: This is "without replacement": 5 choices for captain, then 4 for vice-captain, so 5 × 4 = 20. 25 would allow one person to hold both jobs.

mistakes.B: Step 2: 5 × 5 allows the same player to be captain and vice-captain. Only 4 players are left for vice-captain.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 10 counts pairs without order. Captain Ana with vice Ben is different from captain Ben with vice Ana.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you added 5 + 4. Each captain choice pairs with each vice-captain choice, so multiply.

questions.prompt: In a class, 12 boys have a mean score of 15 and 18 girls have a mean score of 20. What is the mean score of the whole class of 30?
questions.explanation: Totals: 12 × 15 = 180 and 18 × 20 = 360, so 540 ÷ 30 = 18. Averaging the means (17.5) ignores the different group sizes.

mistakes.A: Step 3: you averaged the two means. There are more girls, so their total counts for more.
mistakes.C: Step 1: you multiplied the wrong pairs (12 × 20 and 18 × 15). The 12 boys have the mean of 15.
mistakes.D: Step 3: divide the combined total by the number of students (30), not by 2.

questions.prompt: In a group of 45, 25 are in set A, 20 are in set B and 8 are in neither, as shown in the Venn diagram. A person is chosen at random. What is the probability that they are in A only?
questions.explanation: (25 − x) + x + (20 − x) + 8 = 45 gives x = 8, so A only = 25 − 8 = 17 and P = 17/45. Using 25 counts the overlap too.
steps: Add the regions: (25 − x) + x + (20 − x) + 8 = 45, so 53 − x = 45 and x = 8.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 25/45 is all of A, including the overlap. "A only" leaves the overlap out.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 8 is the overlap (and also the number in neither). "A only" is the part of A outside B.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 12/45 is B only. Use the A side of the diagram.

questions.diagram_alt: A Venn diagram with ξ = 45. Only A is labelled 25 − x, the overlap is x, only B is 20 − x, and 8 are outside both circles.

questions.prompt: A bag holds 3 red (R) and 2 blue (B) counters. Two are taken without replacement, as shown in the tree diagram. What is the probability that at least one counter is blue?
questions.explanation: P(no blue) = P(RR) = 3/5 × 2/4 = 6/20 = 3/10, so P(at least one blue) = 1 − 3/10 = 7/10. Answering 3/10 stops at the opposite event.
steps: "At least one blue" is the opposite of "both red".

mistakes.A: Step 2: 3/10 is P(both red) — the opposite of what is asked. Subtract it from 1.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 2/5 is only "the first counter is blue". At least one blue also includes RB.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used 3/5 × 3/5, which is with replacement. The tree shows 2/4 on the second red branch.

questions.diagram_alt: A tree diagram for two picks without replacement. First pick: R 3/5, B 2/5. After R: R 2/4, B 2/4. After B: R 3/4, B 1/4. Outcomes RR, RB, BR, BB.

questions.prompt:
The back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot shows how long (in minutes) 7 morning and 7 evening trips took:

| Morning leaves | Stem | Evening leaves |
|---|---|---|
| 8 5 2 | 1 | 4 6 |
| 9 4 3 1 | 2 | 2 5 7 |
| | 3 | 3 6 |

Key: 2 | 5 means 25 for Evening, and 1 | 2 means 21 for Morning.

How many minutes longer is the evening median than the morning median?
steps: Morning (left leaves read outwards from the stem): 12, 15, 18, 21, 23, 24, 29 — the 4th of 7 is 21.

mistakes.B: Step 3: 5 is the difference between the ranges (22 − 17). Use the medians.
mistakes.C: Step 3: about 4.4 is the difference between the means. Use the middle (4th) values.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 25 is the evening median on its own. Subtract the morning median.

questions.prompt: In a class, 17 students like only art, 9 like both art and music, 20 like music altogether and 4 like neither. How many students are in the class?
questions.explanation: Music only = 20 − 9 = 11, so the class is 17 + 9 + 11 + 4 = 41. Adding 20 directly (50) counts the 9 twice.
steps: The four regions are: art only, both, music only and neither.
Music only = 20 − 9 = 11 (the 20 includes the 9 who like both).

mistakes.A: Step 2: 20 already includes the 9 who like both. Use music only = 20 − 9.
mistakes.B: Step 3: you forgot the 4 students who like neither. They are still in the class.
mistakes.D: Step 3: you left out the 9 who like both.

questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled and the numbers are added. What is the probability that the total is a multiple of 3?
questions.explanation: Totals 3, 6, 9 and 12 fill 2 + 5 + 4 + 1 = 12 of the 36 cells: 12/36 = 1/3. Forgetting 12 gives 11/36.
steps: Cells: total 3 → 2, total 6 → 5, total 9 → 4, total 12 → 1. That is 12 cells.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you forgot the total 12, which is also a multiple of 3.
mistakes.C: Step 1: the totals 2 to 12 are not equally likely. Count cells in the 36-cell table.
mistakes.D: Step 1: the totals are not equally likely, and 12 is a multiple of 3 too.

questions.prompt: Five numbers have a mean of 10. One of the numbers is increased, and the mean becomes 12. By how much was that number increased?
questions.explanation: Old total 10 × 5 = 50; new total 12 × 5 = 60. Only one number changed, so it went up by 60 − 50 = 10. Choosing 2 forgets that the increase is shared among 5 numbers.
steps: Only one number changed, so it increased by 60 − 50 = 10.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 2 is how much the mean went up. The total went up by 2 for each of the 5 numbers.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 12 is the new mean, not the change in one number.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 60 is the new total. Subtract the old total (50).

questions.prompt: A coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting at least two heads?
questions.explanation: There are 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 outcomes. At least two heads: HHT, HTH, THH and HHH — 4 outcomes, so 4/8 = 1/2. 3/8 forgets HHH.
steps: Three tosses give 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT.
At least two heads: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH — 4 outcomes.

mistakes.B: Step 2: 3/8 is exactly two heads. "At least two" also includes HHH.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 1/8 is three heads only. "At least two" also includes exactly two heads.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 7/8 is "at least one head". You need two or more.

questions.prompt: The Venn diagram shows 36 people. The number in A only is twice the number in B only. 5 are in both and 7 are in neither. A person is chosen at random. What is the probability that they are in set A?
questions.explanation: 2y + 5 + y + 7 = 36 gives 3y = 24, so y = 8. A = 16 + 5 = 21, and P = 21/36 = 7/12. Using 16 forgets the overlap.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 16/36 is A only. Set A also includes the 5 people in both.
mistakes.B: Step 3: 29 is A or B. Leave out the people in B only.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 5 is the overlap only. Set A is A only plus the overlap.

questions.diagram_alt: A Venn diagram with ξ = 36. A only is labelled 2y, the overlap is 5, B only is y, and 7 are outside both circles.
